description: Enter probabilities or counts for A, B, and A and B to see the conditional probability formula applied step by step, with a proportional Venn diagram.

learningObjectives: Calculate P(A | B) and P(B | A) from P(A and B) and the probability of the given event (Apply)
Use counts from a two-way table to calculate a conditional probability (Apply)
Recognize invalid inputs, such as P(A and B) greater than P(B) (Understand)
prerequisites: Basic probability rules and the meaning of "A and B" (Chapter 9)

keyQuestions: Which event is the new sample space?
What do the numerator and denominator count?
commonMisconceptions: P(A | B) is found by dividing by P(A)
P(A | B) and P(B | A) are interchangeable
A conditional probability can be larger than 1
assessmentOpportunities: Student computes a conditional probability by hand and verifies it with the calculator
Student explains each of the three steps in words
Student predicts which of P(A | B) and P(B | A) is larger from the Venn diagram
